item.claim: Body weight decreased by 2.1 kg with drug R and 0.6 kg with placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Body weight, kg, LS mean change (SE) | -2.1 (0.3) | -0.6 (0.3)
result.reason: The table reports week 26 LS mean body-weight changes of −2.1 kg with Drug R and −0.6 kg with placebo.

item.claim: At week 26, drug R reduced HbA1c by 0.94% compared with 0.28% on placebo (difference -0.66%, p < 0.001).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports Week 26 changes of -0.94% with Drug R and -0.28% with placebo, a difference of -0.66% with p < 0.001.

item.claim: More patients discontinued because of adverse events on drug R (6.0%) than on placebo (2.3%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports discontinuation due to TEAEs in 6.0% of patients on Drug R and 2.3% on placebo.

item.claim: Nausea was the most common adverse event with drug R, reported by 12.0% of patients versus 4.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: Nausea is the most frequently reported listed event for Drug R, at 12.0%, versus 4.0% on placebo.

item.claim: Nearly 40% of drug R patients reached HbA1c below 7.0% at week 26, versus about 22% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: At week 26, 39.9% of Drug R patients and 21.8% of placebo patients had HbA1c below 7.0%, matching the claim’s rounded figures.

item.claim: Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates in the two groups (7.0% and 6.4%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports serious TEAEs in 7.0% of the Drug R group and 6.4% of the placebo group, matching the claim.

item.claim: Systolic blood pressure fell numerically more with drug R, but the difference from placebo was not statistically significant (p = 0.247).
item.label: supported

result.reason: Systolic BP decreased numerically more with Drug R than placebo, and the reported p-value is 0.247.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction appeared smaller in patients with eGFR below 60 (difference -0.38%) than in those with eGFR of 60 or above (-0.72%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports differences of -0.38% for eGFR <60 and -0.72% for eGFR >=60, consistent with the claim that the reduction appeared smaller in the lower-eGFR group.

item.claim: Fasting plasma glucose fell by 24.3 mg/dL on drug R versus 8.9 mg/dL on placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Fasting plasma glucose, mg/dL, LS mean change (SE) | -24.3 (2.1) | -8.9 (2.1)
result.reason: The table reports week 26 LS mean changes of −24.3 mg/dL on Drug R and −8.9 mg/dL on placebo.

item.claim: Hypoglycaemia (glucose below 54 mg/dL) was reported in 4.0% of patients on drug R and 1.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports hypoglycaemia below 54 mg/dL in 4.0% of patients on Drug R and 1.0% on placebo.

item.claim: The treatment effect on HbA1c was consistent across age subgroups (interaction p = 0.61).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports an interaction p-value of 0.61 for the age subgroups, supporting the claim that the treatment effect was consistent across them.

item.claim: Shifts in ALT to more than three times the upper limit of normal were rare (0.7% on drug R, 0.3% on placebo).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports shifts to >3x ULN in 0.7% of Drug R recipients and 0.3% of placebo recipients.

item.claim: One patient on drug R and two on placebo died during the study.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports one death on Drug R and two on placebo.

item.claim: Drug R reduced HbA1c significantly more than placebo at every visit through week 52.
item.label: supported

result.reason: At each reported visit through week 52, Drug R had a greater reduction in HbA1c than placebo and the between-group difference was statistically significant (p < 0.001).

item.claim: Drug R did not increase the risk of hypoglycaemia.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Hypoglycaemia was reported more often with Drug R than placebo (4.0% vs 1.0%), so the table does not support the claim that Drug R did not increase its risk.

item.claim: Drug R is safe in patients with renal impairment.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Overview of treatment-emergent adverse events (safety population)
result.reason: The source reports adverse events in the overall safety population and does not establish safety specifically in patients with renal impairment.

item.claim: Gastrointestinal events were mild and transient.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: severity and duration aren't in the table

result.reason: The table reports nausea and diarrhoea frequencies but does not establish that these events were mild or transient.

item.claim: Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups; mean age was 61.2 and 60.8 years and mean HbA1c 8.3% and 8.2%.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports the claimed age and HbA1c means, which are closely similar between groups and support the descriptive characterization as balanced.

item.claim: No safety signals were identified for hepatic or renal function.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: eGFR fell 2.9 vs 1.1; 'no signal' is a conclusion the table can't make

result.reason: The table reports ALT shifts to >3× ULN in both groups and does not establish that no hepatic or renal safety signals were identified.

item.claim: Drug R was well tolerated, with an adverse event profile similar to placebo.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: drug-related 24.0 vs 13.8, discontinuation 6.0 vs 2.3, grade>=3 9.0 vs 6.0

result.quote:
Drug-related TEAE | 72 (24.0) | 41 (13.8)
Grade 3 or higher TEAE | 27 (9.0) | 18 (6.0)
TEAE leading to discontinuation | 18 (6.0) | 7 (2.3)
result.reason: Drug R had notably higher rates of drug-related, severe, and discontinuation-leading adverse events than placebo, so the table does not establish a similar adverse-event profile or that it was well tolerated.

item.claim: The HbA1c benefit of drug R was consistent across renal function subgroups.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The interaction p-value is 0.04 and the eGFR <60 confidence interval includes zero, so the source does not establish a consistent HbA1c benefit across renal function subgroups.

item.claim: In patients with eGFR below 60, drug R significantly reduced HbA1c versus placebo (difference -0.38%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The reported difference is -0.38%, but its 95% CI includes zero, so the table does not establish a significant reduction in this subgroup.

item.claim: At week 52, drug R reduced body weight by 2.1 kg.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Title: Secondary endpoints at week 26 (full analysis set)
result.reason: The cited source reports a 2.1 kg body-weight reduction at week 26, not week 52.

item.claim: Older patients (65 years and above) derived a significantly smaller benefit than younger patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The older group had a numerically smaller treatment benefit, but the interaction p-value of 0.61 does not support a significantly smaller benefit.

item.claim: In the safety population, HbA1c fell by 0.94% at week 26.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Title: Change from baseline in HbA1c (%) by visit (full analysis set, MMRM)
result.reason: The table reports results for the full analysis set, not the safety population, so it does not establish the claim for the stated population.

item.claim: The maximal HbA1c reduction was reached by week 12.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The largest reduction shown occurs at week 26 (-0.94), not week 12 (-0.72).

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction with drug R increased steadily through week 52.
item.label: not_supported

result.location: Table 14.2.1, Week 12, Week 26, and Week 52 rows
result.reason: The reduction is greater at week 26 than week 12, but smaller at week 52 than week 26, so it did not increase steadily through week 52.

item.claim: Drug R also lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Although the estimated reduction was greater with Drug R, the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.247; 95% CI includes zero), so the table does not establish that Drug R lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.

item.claim: Drug R caused urinary tract infections in 5.0% of patients.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: 5.0 vs 4.7 on placebo; incidence isn't causation

result.reason: The table reports urinary tract infections in 5.0% of Drug R patients as treatment-emergent adverse events, but it does not establish that Drug R caused them.

item.claim: Weight loss with drug R was driven by its gastrointestinal effects.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table reports weight loss but provides no evidence that it was driven by gastrointestinal effects.

item.claim: Any adverse event was reported by 57.0% of drug R patients and 61.0% of placebo patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The source reports any TEAE in 61.0% of Drug R patients and 57.0% of placebo patients, the reverse of the claim.

item.claim: Headache was more common with drug R than with placebo (3.7% vs 4.4%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The reported rates show headache was less common with drug R than with placebo, not more common.

item.claim: eGFR increased slightly with drug R over 52 weeks.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The source reports a decrease in eGFR with Drug R over 52 weeks, not an increase.

item.claim: Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 50% more frequent with drug R (9.0% vs 6.0%), all of them drug-related.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: relatedness of grade 3 events not in table

result.reason: The table supports the reported 9.0% versus 6.0% rates, but it does not establish that all Grade 3 or higher events were drug-related.

item.claim: Drug R provides an additional blood pressure benefit of 1.3 mmHg.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The estimated difference is 1.3 mmHg in Drug R’s favor, but its confidence interval includes no difference and p=0.247, so the table does not establish an additional blood pressure benefit.

item.claim: Drug R tripled the proportion of patients reaching HbA1c below 7.0%.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The proportion was 39.9% with Drug R versus 21.8% with placebo, which is not three times as high.

item.claim: Haematocrit decreased with drug R.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Haematocrit increased from baseline with Drug R, with a mean change of +1.9%, rather than decreased.
